title: Pan-Seared Ribeye
description: Butter-basted, dry-brined the night before, rested properly.
source: Sample recipe — replace with the real version from a starred chat

steps.text: The night before: salt the steak generously on all sides and refrigerate uncovered on a rack.
steps.why: The salt pulls moisture out, dissolves, and gets reabsorbed overnight — seasoning deep instead of just the surface. The dry surface it leaves behind is what makes a real crust possible; wet steak steams.

steps.text: Pull the steak 45 minutes before cooking so it loses the fridge chill.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet over high heat until it just smokes. Lay the steak away from you and sear undisturbed, 3 minutes.
Flip. Sear the second side 3 minutes, then flip every minute for even crust.
steps.why: Once each face has color, frequent flipping cooks the interior more evenly than one long sear per side — the temperature gradient stays shallow, so less gray band under the crust.

steps.text: Drop to medium. Add butter, thyme, and garlic; tilt the pan and baste continuously until 125°F internal for medium-rare.
steps.why: Basting bathes the top in hot aromatic fat so the steak cooks from both sides at once, and the browning milk solids season the crust.

steps.text: Rest on a warm plate, loosely tented, 8 minutes.
steps.why: Resting lets the juices thicken and redistribute instead of flooding the cutting board, and carryover heat finishes the center.

notes.title: Pan choice
notes.body: Cast iron or heavy stainless only. A thin pan crashes in temperature the moment the steak lands, and you steam instead of sear.

plating: Slice against the grain, fan on a warm plate, spoon over the thyme-garlic butter, finish with flaky salt.
